content.title: 3 Russell 2000 Stocks We Approach with Caution
content.summary: The Russell 2000 (^RUT) is home to many small-cap stocks, offering investors the chance to uncover hidden gems before the broader market catches on. However, these companies often come with higher volatility and risk, as their smaller size makes them more vulnerable to economic downturns.

content.title: 3 Restaurant Stocks We Think Twice About
content.summary: Restaurants are go-to meeting hubs for friends, family, and colleagues. But the side dish is that they’re quite difficult to operate because high inventory and labor costs generally lead to thin margins at the store level. This leaves little room for error if demand dries up, and it seems like the market has some reservations as the industry has tumbled by 14.4% over the past six months. This performance is a noticeable divergence from the S&P 500’s 15.3% return.

content.summary: Denny's (DENN) reported that earnings have declined at an average annual rate of 11.9% over the past five years, with net profit margins tightening to 2.2% from 3.9% a year ago. Looking ahead, the company is projected to rebound strongly, with earnings expected to grow about 39.8% per year, significantly ahead of the broader US market's 16% forecast, while revenue growth is estimated at a slower 3.4% per year. content.title: Why Denny's Stock Rocketed 50% Higher Today
Denny's (DENN) Stock Trades Up, Here Is Why
content.summary: Shares of diner restaurant chain Denny’s (NASDAQ:DENN) jumped 49.8% in the morning session after the company announced it had agreed to be acquired by a group of investors in an all-cash deal that will take the diner chain private.

content.title: Why Are Kura Sushi (KRUS) Shares Soaring Today
content.summary: Shares of sushi restaurant chain Kura Sushi (NASDAQ:KRUS) jumped 5.5% in the morning session after its stock was lifted by positive sentiment in the restaurant sector after peer Denny's Corp. announced it had agreed to be acquired at a significant premium. The Denny's buyout deal was valued at $620 million, which represented a 52.1% premium to its closing price from the previous session.
